title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: THE FIRST TENT
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Tasha Greene, a forty-four-year-old inspector at a cereal plant in Cedar Rapids, Iowa.
Tasha has never slept one night outside. Not one.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE ASK
segments.quote: Wilderness is not a luxury but a necessity of the human spirit, and as vital to our lives as water and good bread.
segments.author: Edward Abbey
lines: One July Sunday, her dad Clarence, a retired welder of seventy-seven, asked her to take him camping for the August meteor shower.
Tasha said bugs, bears and bathrooms. Clarence tapped an Edward Abbey line taped to his fridge:
Wilderness is not a luxury but a necessity of the human spirit, and as vital to our lives as water and good bread.
So Tasha booked two nights at Ledges State Park.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE GEAR
segments.quote: Let your boat of life be light, packed with only what you need.
segments.author: Jerome K. Jerome
lines: Tasha packed three flashlights, a first aid kit the size of a suitcase, and bear spray. In Iowa.
The trunk would not close. Clarence opened a book by the English humorist Jerome K. Jerome:
Let your boat of life be light, packed with only what you need.
She left the bear spray on the kitchen table.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE STORM
segments.quote: Any man may be in good spirits and good temper when he's well dressed.
segments.author: Charles Dickens
lines: At midnight a thunderstorm hit, and the tent folded on them like a wet taco.
Tasha was soaked. Clarence was grinning. He quoted cheerful Mark Tapley, from Charles Dickens:
Any man may be in good spirits and good temper when he's well dressed.
So Tasha laughed, wrung out her socks, and they slept in the car, snoring in stereo.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: SOGGY MORNING
segments.quote: There is no duty we so much underrate as the duty of being happy.
segments.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
lines: Morning was gray and drippy. Every camper looked grumpy. Tasha wanted to go home.
Then she remembered a Robert Louis Stevenson line on a coffee mug at work:
There is no duty we so much underrate as the duty of being happy.
So she made pancakes. For everyone. Twelve wet strangers, laughing around one tiny skillet.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE CLOUDS
segments.quote: How poor are they that have not patience! What wound did ever heal but by degrees?
segments.author: William Shakespeare
lines: Night two, clouds. No stars. Tasha checked her weather app every two minutes and wanted to pack up.
Clarence pulled his blanket tighter and quoted Shakespeare:
How poor are they that have not patience! What wound did ever heal but by degrees?
So she put the phone away, and they listened to the owls.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE SKY
segments.quote: Try and leave this world a little better than you found it.
segments.author: Robert Baden-Powell
lines: At three in the morning the clouds slid away. Shooting stars! Clarence counted forty-one. Tasha counted forty-one, plus one airplane.
At sunrise she picked up every bottle cap around their site, and Clarence quoted the founder of the Scouts, Robert Baden-Powell:
Try and leave this world a little better than you found it.
Now Tasha owns a tent. Next August is booked, and the pancake crowd is coming too.

segments.head: SIX WISE WORDS
segments.quote: Go outside. Pack light. Laugh. Be happy. Wait. Leave it better.
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: So get outside, pack light, laugh in the rain, choose happy, be patient, and leave it better.
Me? I went camping once. I brought a recliner.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
